result.title: The Race Is Decided Early! A Kernel Law Predicts Lock-In in Majority-Vote Test-Time RL
result.summary: Test-time reinforcement learning with majority-vote rewards trains a language model on unlabeled questions by rewarding the samples that agree with its most frequent answer. During training, each question locks into one answer, on hard questions often a wrong one, but which answer it locks into is known only after training. In this paper, we show that this outcome is decided early, in a short race driven by sampling noise between the answers that are close at the start, and we derive the probability of each outcome. With a separate logit for each answer, the runner-up wins with a normal tail probability of the initial gap, scaled by an explicit noise constant. In a network, however, the answer logits depend on shared parameters, and through the kernel of these parameters the updates of the trailing answers also change the gap of the two leaders. This spillover shifts the boundary between the starts won by each leader, and a closed form computes the shifted probability from a kernel probe and the start logits. In LoRA experiments with three models from two families, predictions made before training with the kernel frozen at its start value forecast which answer each question locks into better than a logistic model refitted on the outcomes, although they use no fitted constants. The closed form matches these predictions on the runs in which a check before training finds that the two leaders stay above the other answers, and it explains why a law that ignores the spillover needs a strongly inflated step.

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析多数投票奖励的测试时强化学习中「每个问题锁定到某个答案」的现象，提出锁定由训练早期采样噪声驱动的短程「竞赛」决定，并给出基于初始 logit 差与参数核的闭式概率预测，在 LoRA 实验中用冻结于初始值的核在训练前预测锁定答案。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本 TTRL，但其「用初始状态与参数核几何预测轨迹早期锁定」的线索，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 轨迹或答案承诺能否在推理早期通过与表示耦合关系预测，以及核外溢效应如何影响状态更新与贡献分配。
